title: Add the camera measurement
summary: Give each camera tag solution to the pose estimator, then see how close the estimate gets.

say.never: `LocalizationSubsystem` already asks MW-Lib's proxy server for the camera **tag solutions** and loops over the new, sensible ones. Nothing hands them to the pose estimator yet, so the estimate is just odometry. You will add one call, `addVisionMeasurement(...)`, and then pick how much to trust the cameras.
say.bit: The tag solutions are collected but never given to the estimator. Add one call, then choose the trust.

say.bit: The call takes: the pose, the picture's time, and the standard deviations.

say.never: In the simulator there are no real cameras, so a provided piece plays the camera computers: it sends tag solutions into MW-Lib's **proxy server**, the same place a real robot's camera computers send theirs. MW-Lib logs what the proxy server holds under **Proxy/TagSolutions**. In **AdvantageScope**, search for `TagSolutions` and look at it while the robot is in view of some tags. Each solution has a pose, the time of its picture, the camera and the ids of the tags it used. Two or more ids means a multi-tag solution, which is the accurate kind. You may also see an alert saying the proxy server has no clients: that is normal here. Click **I did it** when you have looked.
say.bit: Simulated cameras send tag solutions through MW-Lib's proxy server, like real camera computers. Look at **Proxy/TagSolutions** in AdvantageScope: pose, time and tag ids. Two or more ids is accurate. Click I did it.

steps.title: Optional: see the tags the cameras use

say.never: If you like, see which AprilTags the cameras are using right now. `LocalizationSubsystem` logs them as **Subsystem/Localization/VisibleTags**. In **AdvantageScope**, open the **3D Field** tab (or the **2D Field**), search for `VisibleTags` and drag it onto **Vision Targets**. The tags light up while a camera sees them. Drive around and watch them change. Click **I did it** when you have looked, or to skip this.

say.never: Drive around with **W**, **A**, **S** and **D**, for more than 5 meters in total. Then let go and wait 2 seconds without touching anything. The check only judges the estimate after the robot has sat still, because a moving robot is always a little behind. Click **I did it** after you have waited.

say.never: Look at the error plot. While you drive it jumps around a little. Once you stopped it should settle to just a few centimeters, well under the 5 cm limit. If it stays large, the cameras are being ignored (numbers too big) or something in the call is wrong.
say.bit: The error should settle to a few centimeters once you stop. If not, the trust numbers or the call are off.

say.never: Click the lesson chip and press **Verify**. The first checkpoint looks at your code. The estimate checkpoint only passes after you have driven more than 5 meters and stopped for 2 seconds, so do that first if it still fails.
say.bit: Press **Verify**. The estimate check needs more than 5 m driven, then 2 s of standing still.
